```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def solve(prices, split_factors):
    # Ensure prices and split_factors have the same shape and columns
    if prices.shape != split_factors.shape or not all(prices.columns == split_factors.columns):
        raise ValueError("prices and split_factors must have the same shape and columns")
    
    # Initialize the result DataFrame with zeros
    weights = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=prices.index, columns=prices.columns)
    
    # Iterate over each asset column
    for col in prices.columns:
        # Calculate the simple returns for the current asset
        returns = prices[col].pct_change().dropna()
        
        # Calculate the inverse sample standard deviation (ddof=1)
        inv_std_devs = 1 / returns.std(ddof=1)
        
        # Normalize the inverse standard deviations to sum to 1
        normalized_weights = inv_std_devs / inv_std_devs.sum()
        
        # Assign the normalized weights to the corresponding column in the result DataFrame
        weights[col] = normalized_weights
    
    # Set weights for rows before the 61st row to zero
    weights.iloc[:61] = 0
    
    return weights
```
